{{See also|Upcoming features|Matcha Flavoured 1.12.2#Post-release fixes}}
This page lists '''known bugs''' in [[Matcha Flavoured]]: places where the pack's code does something it evidently isn't meant to, such as text that shows a raw translation key, tooltips that disagree with an item's real values, and mechanics that don't match the release notes. Each entry was found by reading the pack's source for the current release, {{Version|1.12.2}}-beta. Bugs that the repository's <code>main</code> branch has already fixed are still in the release; they are listed under [[#Fixed on the main branch|Fixed on the main branch]] until the next version comes out. The README asks players to report bugs through the feedback form it links.<ref>{{Source|README.md}}</ref> Bugs fixed in earlier versions are listed in each article's History section and on the [[Version history|version pages]].

== Untranslated text ==
When a text component asks for a translation key that the resource pack's language file doesn't define, the game shows the key itself. The following keys are used by the datapack but missing from <code>en_us.json</code>:<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/lang/en_us.json}}</ref>
{| class="wikitable"
! Where it shows !! Missing key !! Notes
|-
| Name of the [[Elytra#Hepatizon Elytra|hepatizon elytra]] || <code>item.kleispack.hepatizon_elytra</code> || The language file names the item under the older key <code>item.kleispack.bronze_elytra</code> ("Hepatizon Elytra"), which the recipe and loot table no longer use.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/hepatizon_elytra.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/equipment/hepatizon/elytra.json}}</ref>
|-
| "Repaired with" line of the [[Elytra#Shakudo Elytra|shakudo elytra]] || <code>item.minecraft.copper_block</code> || The vanilla key is <code>block.minecraft.copper_block</code>, which the hepatizon elytra uses correctly.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/shakudo_elytra.json}}</ref>
|-
| Name and tooltip of six [[bulk blocks]] (terracotta, malachite, cinnabar, blackstone, smooth basalt, smooth quartz) || <code>item.kleispack.trade.bulk_terracotta</code>, <code>…bulk_prismarine</code>, <code>…bulk_cinnabar</code>, <code>…bulk_blackstone</code>, <code>…bulk_smooth_basalt</code>, <code>…bulk_smooth_quartz</code> and their <code>.desc</code> keys || Sold by the [[Mason]]. The other bulk blocks have names.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/villager_trade/mason/2/terracotta.json}}</ref>
|-
| Stored-enchantment line of adamant tools || <code>enchantment.kleispack.smelting</code> || The description of the <code>matcha:adamant_tool</code> smelting intrinsic, which every adamant tool carries as a stored enchantment.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/enchantment/adamant_tool.json}}</ref> See [[Adamant equipment]].
|-
| Nowhere in practice || <code>item.kleispack.fish.axolotl</code> || Used by the loot table <code>gameplay/fishing/fish/axolotl</code>, which no other table calls. Fished axolotls come from the junk table and use <code>item.kleispack.axolotl</code>, which exists.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/fish/axolotl.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/junk.json}}</ref>
|}

Each item's article cites the file. Other tooltip problems:
* The [[Elytra#Shakudo Elytra|shakudo elytra]]'s tooltip promises an "Elytra Bonus" of 10 seconds off the shakudo regeneration timer, but the item carries the ordinary shakudo armor intrinsic, so it only counts as one more shakudo piece. A separate <code>matcha:shakudo_elytra</code> intrinsic exists but isn't on the item.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/shakudo_elytra.json}}</ref> The in-development changelog lists "Shakudo Elytra Bonus was not working" as fixed.<ref>{{Cite changelog|quote=Shakudo Elytra Bonus was not working (not sure how this was deleted)}}</ref>
* The [[Adamant Pickaxe|adamant pickaxe]] lists [[divinity]] under "Set Bonus:", but tools don't count toward the set bonus. See [[Divinity]].

== Mechanics ==
* '''Fortune on tomatoes and chorus plants.''' The {{Version|1.12.2}} notes say Fortune now works on tomatoes, glow berry vines and chorus plants.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.2|quote=Fortune now works on: Tomatoes, Glow berry vines, Chorus Plant}}</ref> In the tomato and chorus plant tables, a fixed count is set ''after'' the Fortune and electrum bonuses, which replaces them, so neither has any effect there. It does work on cave vines.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/beetroots.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/chorus_plant.json}}</ref>
* '''Glow berries from bare vines.''' The cave vine tables have no check for whether the vine carries berries, unlike vanilla, so every broken cave vine block drops glow berries.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/cave_vines.json}}</ref>
* '''Silent fished crystal hearts.''' The treasure sound checks for the item model <code>matcha:crystal_heart</code>, but fished [[Crystal Heart|crystal hearts]] use <code>matcha:heart_container</code>, so catching one plays no sound. See [[Fishing sounds#Bugs]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/fishing_sounds/treasure.json}}</ref>
* '''Incomplete Angler's Almanac.''' The junk category of the [[Angler's Almanac]] has entries for a bowl and a tripwire hook, but no fishing table can give either, so the tab can't be completed.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/anglers_almanac/junk/bowl.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/junk.json}}</ref>
* '''Iron chain recipe never unlocks.''' Picking up iron ingots is meant to unlock the recipe that turns 3 iron ingots into 18 [[chain]]s, but the unlock names <code>iron_chain_from_iron</code>, while the recipe is <code>iron_chain_from_ingot</code>. The recipe works when placed by hand but never appears in the recipe book.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/recipe_unlocks/iron_ingot.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/iron_chain_from_ingot.json}}</ref>
* '''Early pickaxes mine ancient debris.''' The pack's pickaxes list <code>#minecraft:mineable/pickaxe</code> as correct for drops without a tier check, and the blocks each tier ''can't'' mine are listed by hand. Ancient debris isn't on any of those lists, so even a wooden pickaxe gets it. See [[Tools#Mining levels]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/tags/block/non_mineable/wood.json}}</ref>
* '''Cut diamonds in village chests.''' The 1.12.2 notes say no "naturally-occuring free diamonds" should appear in surface structures, but the village toolsmith and weaponsmith chest tables still contain cut diamonds. (The desert pyramid gives raw diamonds.)<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/chests/village/village_toolsmith.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/chests/village/village_weaponsmith.json}}</ref> See [[Chest loot]].
* '''Mobs keep their spawn equipment drops.''' The pack means to set the drop chances of the armor and weapons that hostile mobs spawn with to 0, but the command targets <code>@n</code> (the nearest matching mob) from a function that runs as the new mob without running at its position, so it changes the matching mob nearest the world spawn point instead. Most mobs keep their vanilla chance to drop that gear. See [[Spawning]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/spawn_mechanic/clear_drop_chances.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/spawn_mechanic/check_mob_spawn.mcfunction}}</ref>
* '''Invisible sturdy leather armor from tanneries.''' The [[Sturdy leather armor|sturdy leather armor]] found in village tannery chests has the equipment asset <code>minecraft:sturdy_leather</code>, but the resource pack defines it as <code>matcha:sturdy_leather</code>, so these pieces are invisible when worn. Crafted pieces use the right asset. This is not fixed on <code>main</code> either.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/chests/equipment/sturdy_leather.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/matcha/equipment/sturdy_leather.json}}</ref>
* '''Glass bottles lost when crafting cheese and stroganoff.''' The advancement that gives back a milk bottle's or oil's glass bottle after crafting lists cheese under its old recipe ID <code>main:food/crafting/cheese</code>, and doesn't list stroganoff, toadstool stroganoff or crimson stroganoff at all, so crafting any of these uses up the bottle. This is not fixed on <code>main</code> either. In 1.12.2-beta most other food recipes lose their bottle too; see [[#Fixed on the main branch|below]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/mechanics/glass_bottle_from_crafting.json}}</ref>

== Other ==
* The chat message shown when the pack loads reports "version 1.12.1", although the release is 1.12.2 and the internal version number is 1122.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/setup/load.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/setup/scoreboard/create_scoreboards.mcfunction}}</ref>

== Fixed on the main branch ==
The following bugs are in 1.12.2-beta. The repository's <code>main</code> branch has fixed them since the release, so they should be gone in the next version; until then they affect every game. The fixes are listed on [[Matcha Flavoured 1.12.2#Post-release fixes]].

=== Advancements ===
* '''"Crystal Heart!" can't be earned.''' The advancement looks for an item whose model is <code>heart_container</code>, which the game reads as <code>minecraft:heart_container</code>. Crystal hearts use <code>matcha:heart_container</code>, so the advancement and its 3 obols are never granted.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/tutorial/obtain_heart.json}}</ref> See [[Crystal Heart]].
* '''Pufferfish missing from the Angler's Almanac.''' The Hot Saltwater pufferfish entry checks for the model <code>matcha:pufferfish</code>, but caught pufferfish keep the vanilla model, so the entry can't be unlocked. The Hot Saltwater entries after it can still be earned.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/anglers_almanac/saltwater/hot/pufferfish.json}}</ref> See [[Angler's Almanac]].

=== Crafting ===
* '''Glass bottles lost when crafting most foods.''' Besides cheese and the stroganoffs (above), the bottle-returning advancement names most food recipes and the hell-bound book by their old <code>main:</code> and <code>blessings:</code> recipe IDs, so crafting them uses up the glass bottle of their water bottle, [[Milk Bottle|milk bottle]], [[oil]] or [[benzene]]. This affects [[Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal|apple cinnamon oatmeal]], [[Buñuelo|buñuelos]], [[cake]], [[Chicken Nugget|chicken nuggets]], [[Chorus Mochi|chorus mochi]], [[dough]] made with a water bottle, [[Fish and Chips|fish and chips]], [[gimmari]], [[Glow Berry Crumble|glow berry crumble]], the [[Hell-Bound Book|hell-bound book]], [[Ice Cream|ice cream]], [[latke]]s, [[lumpia]], [[pupusa]]s, [[seitan]], [[Warped Stroganoff|warped stroganoff]], and curry and ramen [[stock]]. Crafts that use the <code>matcha:</code> IDs, such as flower cloning, [[mud]], concrete, [[phosphor]] and [[Stabilized Estus|stabilized estus]], do return the bottle.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/mechanics/glass_bottle_from_crafting.json}}</ref> See [[Glass Bottle#Returned from crafting]].

=== Mechanics ===
* '''Wither meter shared by all players.''' Each second, the check for a withered player adds 1 to ''every'' player's Wither count and shows the meter in every player's action bar. In multiplayer, players who aren't withered see the meter, and when several players are withered at once their counts rise faster, so they lose hearts in fewer than 8 seconds.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/wither_effect/check_wither_timer.mcfunction}}</ref> See [[Wither effect]].
* '''Freezing water affects spectators.''' The check excludes only Creative mode, so a player in Spectator mode with their head in frozen water gets Slowness, Darkness and damage.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/environmental/check_freezing_water_conditions.mcfunction}}</ref> See [[Freezing water]].
* '''Creative checks fail in multiplayer.''' The functions that turn [[Raw Estus|raw estus]] into Estus Ash and swap water bottles for stackable ones are meant to skip players in Creative mode, but they only check that ''some'' player isn't in Creative mode. On a server with a player in another mode, Creative players are processed too, which is the duplication the check was added to prevent. The estus function also converts raw estus for every player who holds some, not just the one whose inventory changed.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/estus/check_if_estus_should_be_processed.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/estus/process_estus.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/water_bottle/check_if_water_bottle_should_be_processed.mcfunction}}</ref>
* '''Gold ore ignores electrum.''' When stone gold ore drops raw gold, the Fortune bonus is applied twice and the [[Electrum equipment|electrum]] tools' ore bonus not at all. Deepslate gold ore applies each once.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/gold_ore.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/deepslate_gold_ore.json}}</ref>
* '''Five blessings store old enchantments.''' The [[Prayer of Demeter]], [[Prayer of Will]], [[Prayer of St. Clement]], [[Prayer of Aeolus]] and [[Elegy of Hyacinthus]] store Frost Protection, Reach, Trailblaze, Anemos and Zephyr under their old <code>main</code> namespace IDs. Those leftover enchantments exist only to convert items from older versions: their tooltip line reads "ERROR: Please wear me to update" (or "hold me" for Anemos), and they turn into the current enchantment one level per tick while the item is worn, or held for Anemos. The converted levels are added to any the item already has, so they can exceed the normal maximum; two Elegies of Hyacinthus can't be combined into Zephyr II; and Anemos can't be applied to copper swords.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/blessing/frost_walker_frost_protection.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/main/enchantment/freezing_protection.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/main/item_modifier/update_freezing_protection.json}}</ref> See [[Blessing#Old enchantment ids]].

=== Items and textures ===
* '''Steel armor is invisible when worn.''' Its equipment asset is <code>minecraft:steel</code>, but the resource pack defines it as <code>matcha:steel</code>.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/steel_chestplate.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/matcha/equipment/steel.json}}</ref> See [[Steel equipment]].
* '''Steel pickaxe and shovel tooltips.''' Unlike the other steel tools, they don't hide the game's own attribute lines, so the real values appear below the hand-written ones.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/steel_pickaxe.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/steel_shovel.json}}</ref>
* '''Wrong repair materials.''' The [[Adamant Leggings|adamant leggings]] are repaired with a diamond block or a gold block, although the tooltip and the rest of the set use [[Adamant Scrap|adamant scrap]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/adamant_leggings.json}}</ref> [[Shepherd's Shears|Shepherd's shears]] are repaired with iron nuggets or iron ingots, although the tooltip says a copper block.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/villager_trade/shepherd/2/shepherds_shears.json}}</ref>
* '''Untranslated intrinsic lines.''' The stored-enchantment lines of [[Electrum equipment|electrum]] tools and of [[Shakudo equipment|shakudo]] swords, axes and spears show the raw keys <code>enchantment.kleispack.electrum_tool</code> and <code>enchantment.kleispack.shakudo_weapon</code>. The language file defines neither; it still has the shakudo key under its older name, <code>enchantment.kleispack.sanguine</code>.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/lang/en_us.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/enchantment/electrum_tool.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/enchantment/shakudo_weapon.json}}</ref>
* '''Fish bones from Sulfur Caves have no texture.''' The Sulfur Caves fishing table gives [[Fish Bones|fish bones]] the model <code>fish_bones</code> (read as <code>minecraft:fish_bones</code>) instead of <code>matcha:fish_bones</code>, so they show the missing-model texture and don't stack with fish bones from the junk table.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/sulfur_caves.json}}</ref>
* '''Igloo splash potion.''' The splash [[Pickled Crimson Fungus|pickled crimson fungus]] in the [[igloo]] basement's brewing stand uses the model <code>minecraft:pickled_crimson_fungus</code>, which the resource pack doesn't have (its model is in the <code>matcha</code> namespace), so it shows no proper texture.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/structure/igloo/bottom.nbt}}</ref>
* '''Chocolate looks like mushroom stew.''' The resource pack's chocolate model is saved as <code>matcha:item/mushroom_stew</code>, which nothing uses, so [[chocolate]] keeps the vanilla mushroom stew texture.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/matcha/models/item/mushroom_stew.json}}</ref>
* '''<code>/trigger update_item</code> identifies some items by ID.''' Besides translation keys, the update function looks up 85 items by their item ID, and an ID match overrides a key match. A custom item built on one of those vanilla items is rebuilt as that one entry; for example, every splash potion becomes a [[Pickled Warped Fungus|pickled warped fungus]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/update_old_items/update_held_item.mcfunction}}</ref> See [[Updating items]].

== Acknowledged by the developer ==
The README lists one major known bug: on Purpur servers, and possibly others, <code>keep_inventory</code> is handled per dimension, so it has to be set by command in each dimension or items are lost on death.<ref>{{Source|README.md}}</ref> See [[Multiplayer]].

The in-development changelog lists these as low-priority bugs that aren't fixed yet:<ref>{{Cite changelog|quote=Add predicate for surface spawn that excludes structures}}</ref>
* The post-dragon [[Surface|safe-surface]] check doesn't exclude structures in general (only trial chambers and the [[Abbey]] are exempt).
* [[Trailblaze]] boots give their speed boost on mud brick slabs when jumping, but not when simply running on them.
* The toolsmith's hero-of-the-village gift is still stone tools, which the pack otherwise removes.
